solo90.name: Pausa

lines.en: Today we review linking words. Although many students know the basics, they often forget how to connect contrast and reason.
lines.pt: Hoje revisamos conectores. Embora muitos alunos saibam o básico, eles esquecem como ligar contraste e razão.

lines.en: I use because and but all the time, so my essays sound repetitive. How can I vary them?
lines.pt: Eu uso because e but o tempo todo, então minhas redações parecem repetitivas. Como posso variá-los?

lines.en: For contrast, try although, whereas or however. Although it rained all day, we still enjoyed the trip to the coast.
lines.pt: Para contraste, tente although, whereas ou however. Embora tenha chovido o dia todo, ainda aproveitamos a viagem ao litoral.

lines.en: And what about despite? I always confuse it with although. Can I say despite it was raining, or is that wrong?
lines.pt: E despite? Sempre confundo com although. Posso dizer despite it was raining, ou está errado?

lines.en: That is wrong. After despite we need a noun phrase: despite the rain, or in spite of the rain.
lines.pt: Está errado. Depois de despite precisamos de um substantivo ou uma forma -ing: despite the rain, ou in spite of the rain.

lines.en: I see. Now causes: I know because and since. Is as a good option, or does it sound too informal?
lines.pt: Entendi. Agora as causas: conheço because e since. As é uma boa opção, ou soa informal demais?

lines.en: As is fine in writing, and due to is more formal: due to the strike, the trains were late.
lines.pt: As está bem na escrita, e due to é mais formal: due to the strike, the trains were late.

lines.en: What about results? I want to say that something happened and then show the consequence, like a chain of events.
lines.pt: E os resultados? Quero dizer que algo aconteceu e depois mostrar a consequência, como uma cadeia de eventos.

lines.en: Use so, therefore or as a result. The factory closed; as a result, many people lost their jobs, which worried the town.
lines.pt: Use so, therefore ou as a result. A fábrica fechou; como resultado, muitas pessoas perderam o emprego, o que preocupou a cidade.

lines.en: That is useful. So, although the exam is difficult, I can pass because I have practiced these words a lot.
lines.pt: Isso é útil. Então, embora a prova seja difícil, posso passar porque pratiquei muito estas palavras.

lines.en: Exactly. Now write a paragraph with one contrast, one reason and one result, and bring it to class tomorrow.
lines.pt: Exatamente. Agora escreva um parágrafo com um contraste, uma razão e um resultado, e traga para a aula amanhã.

teach.goal: Abrir a aula: objetivo e primeira hipótese.

facts.label: although, despite, however, whereas
facts.sub: Although it rained, we left (oração). Despite the rain, we left (substantivo). However começa nova frase e whereas compara duas coisas.

facts.label: because, since, as, due to
facts.sub: Because + oração; due to / because of + substantivo. Due to the strike, trains were late. As e since soam naturais na escrita.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Although is followed by a clause.
Despite it was raining is correct.
items.why: Use despite the rain or although it was raining.

items.s: Due to is followed by a noun.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Although is followed by a clause. → Verdadeiro (Although it rained.)
Despite it was raining is correct. → Falso (Use despite the rain or although it was raining.)
Due to is followed by a noun. → Verdadeiro (Due to the strike.)

paragraphs: Ben studies English in Houston. He has a big exam next week. His essays sound simple and repetitive. Alma is his teacher. She plans a review of linking words. Ben takes notes carefully.

“Today we review linking words. Although many students know the basics, they often forget how to connect contrast and reason.” says Alma. “I use because and but all the time, so my essays sound repetitive. How can I vary them?” says Ben. “For contrast, try although, whereas or however. Although it rained all day, we still enjoyed the trip to the coast.” says Alma.
